data.name: Campaign Guide — Current Canon
entries: {@i No Cause for Alarm: Ruins of Bellweather} is an active D&D campaign. Four level-4 PCs are about to begin Session 5. Read this current canon before preparing; played events and explicit DM corrections override abandoned plans.

entries.name: Authority and Preparation
entries: {@b PLAYED} = occurred at the table. {@b ESTABLISHED} = explicitly set by DM. {@b PREPARED} = future premise but not yet played. {@b OPEN} = uncertain and must not be invented as already true.

The former live campaign is preserved unchanged on GitHub branch archive/pre-nov-2026-canon-reset. That archive is not active canon. Only location geography/maps, selected useful rules, shops, established personal history, and actual play are carried forward.

The DM prepares deeply to understand the DNA of the world, then improvises NPC and world responses. Do not replace comprehensive preparation with a short scene script. Build maps, routines, motivations, checks, encounters, stats, consequences, and test the material.
The world exists independently of the PCs; people have jobs, disputes, relationships and priorities of their own. Not every person, site, or event relates to the central conflict.
Do not decide outcomes or destinies in advance. The party can accept or refuse jobs, split up, negotiate, sneak, attack, retreat or invent a different answer.

entries.name: The World — ESTABLISHED
entries: The Free City of Bellweather was sold by its Council to the Crown while the party was at Kellan's Well. Every Council member, including Perrin Cardon, departed after the sale. The Council no longer governs.

King Hendrix Stucky rules from the capital. His son Prince Reginald Stucky and Reginald's wife Princess Narcia Stucky govern Bellweather. The royals are comically entitled and cruel, but the government has real power and coherent administrators.
Koven House is the Crown's municipal headquarters and records office. Ledger House remains independent and under Brakkus Ledgerhelm. Bishop Brann stayed in Bellweather.
Cardon Weavehouse is OWNED BY THE CROWN, despite its old name. Perrin has no current ownership claim. The Crown employs a coercive indentured labor system there.

Jaroood is a 243-year-old HIGH ELF who came to Bellweather with Prince Reginald. He has COMPLETE OPERATIONAL CONTROL of the Crown-owned Weavehouse: staff, shifts, discipline, worker assignments, admissions, debt assessments, records and releases. He believes the Crown's debt-based slavery is justified, personally earns 10% of EACH ADDITIONAL DEBT ASSESSMENT beyond a worker's original principal, and remains loyal because the Crown enriches and protects him. He fears only losing Crown favor. His voice is a younger, vigorous Mr. Burns, nasal and condescending without frailty. He stands 5 ft. 11 in., slender, with pale gold eyes, narrow face, slicked-back silver-blond hair, burgundy coat and ivory waistcoat.
Brakkus is a half-orc retired level-16 Oath of Devotion paladin of Oghma, not of any other god. His mother Elena was a librarian who taught him to read and understand people before judging them.
Bishop Brann proposed that the PCs outwardly cooperate with the Crown while secretly passing information to him and Brakkus. Opposition is beginning, not an already established spy organization.

The Radiant Well is a real magical phenomenon below the surface, relevant to the old legend Brakkus told about possible influence over minds. Its nature, access route, and any Crown connection are OPEN, not automatic campaign answers.

entries.name: Campaign Play Standard
entries: Give named NPCs established physical descriptions and reliable portrayal cues on their first appearance. Let them react according to beliefs, information and circumstances.
Preserve all established shop catalogs and the approved Bellweather Crown-era overview and Ledger House map.
Future chapter locations remain. Former events, enemy lineups, property disputes, treasure placements, villains, predetermined advancement and finales are not current canon.

entries.name: Historical Position
entries: The campaign opened with the storm and the adventurers' arrival around Bellweather. Ledger House became the party's home base.
The old playable encounter outline is archived. It does not imply every originally drafted beat occurred.

entries.name: Current Conditions
entries: Use the approved Crown-era Bellweather map, including the established South Ward, Maren Isle, surrounding geography and existing landmarks. Do not redraw its basic geography.
Crown authority operates through Koven House. Ledger House is independently run by Brakkus. Shops and citizens have their own lives and may have differing reactions to the takeover.
A building shown on an old map remains a location; its former proposed owners, occupants and encounter scripts do not.

entries.name: Historical Position
entries: The party's earlier city exploration included the Slums; what was formerly the Slums is reflected in the South Ward of the approved city map.
The party helped traveling merchant Jord recover a strongbox and missing horse; his promised discount remains. Previous unplayed encounters are archived.

entries.name: Established Outcomes
entries: The party freed seven captives: Nela Orr, Council surveyors Lessa Dorn and Kav Orin, three other temple caretakers and a wounded temple guard.
Tal Rusk and remaining opponents were killed; the recovered reliquary went to Bishop Brann. The coded ledger, spyglass and compass passed into Council custody before the Council departed.
The PCs reached level 4 after Blackstone.
The former Council sentenced Pepper for killing Kaleb to five service missions: Kellan's Well unpaid, four subsequent paid missions. That sentence has never been formally discharged.

entries.name: Established Outcomes
entries: The four level-4 adventurers stopped the alarm runner with Tasha's Hideous Laughter. Fog Cloud interfered with Bow Gallery defenders; three Scouts were encountered there.
Aaron read a Ranger's surface thoughts, learning information about Noren concealed by the Ranger's spoken responses. Arunem broke through the ceiling to flank Noren and his Warrior Veteran.
Noren Vale was leader of the Iron Covenant and revealed the impending Crown takeover to save himself. The party bound him and the Veteran. Their deaths occurred in the next session.
The Decanter of Endless Water was recovered and went to Pepper. Jarrock's drinking and Pepper's refusal to heal him were player-driven moments.
The proposed sluice repair was removed. The mission counted as COMPLETE without restoring a sluice. No automatic level-up beyond level 4 is established.

data.name: Chapter 6: Bellweather Under the Crown — Session 4 Record / Session 5 Launch

entries.name: Session 5 — Opening Recap Monologue (TEMPORARY: REMOVE AFTER SESSION)
entries: {@b Read aloud before the opening scene. Temporary section: remove after Session 5 is played.}
Our story began during a terrible storm.
Four strangers found themselves in the city of Bellweather, a free city governed by a council, where they took shelter at an inn called Ledger House.
There, they met Brakkus Ledgerhelm, a retired paladin of Oghma who had traded his sword for the responsibilities of running an inn.
Over the following days, Pepper, Jarrock, Aaron, and Arunem began making a name for themselves in Bellweather.
They explored the city's slums, helped a traveling merchant named Jord recover his stolen horse and strongbox, and eventually became involved in the affairs of the city council.
That involvement would become considerably more complicated when Pepper killed a man named Kaleb.
The council held Pepper responsible and sentenced her to five missions of service to the city.

But first, the party was sent to Blackstone Temple, where they discovered seven people being held captive. They fought their way through the temple, rescued the prisoners, and recovered a religious artifact that they returned to Bishop Brann.
Their next assignment took them to Kellan's Well.
There, they confronted members of a criminal organization known as the Iron Covenant, eventually capturing its leader, Noren Vale.
But Noren had something to tell them.
The city council was planning to sell Bellweather to a monarchy.
And when the adventurers returned to the city, they discovered that he had been telling the truth.
The council was gone.
Bellweather had been sold to the Stucky Crown.

The royal family had taken control of the government, its buildings, and its institutions. Royal soldiers patrolled the streets, and contracts once held by the council were now being enforced in the name of the King.
The party's first few hours under royal rule were... eventful.
Noren and his surviving guard were killed. The guard's headless body was stuffed into a bag, and a brief encounter with the city watch confirmed that Bellweather's old government no longer existed.
Pepper, meanwhile, decided to do some shopping.
Following an unfortunate disagreement with a merchant, she visited the new royal headquarters to file a complaint.
Unfortunately for Pepper, the guards discovered her outstanding service contract.
Instead of helping her with her complaint, they arrested her and prepared to send her to the southern ruins for forced labor.
Brakkus intervened, negotiating her release into his personal custody.

Later, Bishop Brann explained what had happened to the city. He had refused to accept payment from its sale, and he proposed that the adventurers maintain the appearance of cooperating with the Crown while quietly helping him learn what its new rulers were doing.
And then another visitor arrived.
Tulcornix Avemvir, the adopted brother of the man Pepper had killed, came looking for help.
Kaleb had left behind a widow named Elowen.
She was being held at Cardon Weavehouse, a textile factory now controlled by the Crown, where debts and mounting fees had trapped her in forced service.
Whatever the party's feelings about Kaleb, Elowen was still there, and Tulcornix wanted her brought home.
The adventurers began discussing how they might get her out.
Aaron sent his familiar, Drysa, to observe the Weavehouse overnight.
And that brings us to this morning.
Bellweather is waking beneath the banners of its new rulers. Workers are heading to their jobs, royal soldiers are taking up their posts, and the people of the city are going about their lives.
At Ledger House, Brakkus has breakfast underway, and the adventurers have a decision to make.
But they're not the only travelers whose journeys have brought them to Bellweather.
And that's where we begin Session 5.

entries.name: Session 5 — At Ledger House
entries: Morning at Ledger House: breakfast is underway, Brakkus tends the bar, and Drysa returns from watching the Weavehouse. The party is preparing to rescue Elowen.

At the inn: Drysa reports, Detritus arrives seeking information, Jord comes looking for lodging after the Crown requisitioned his hotel, and Brakkus invites Aaron for a private talk. Common room and porch for arrivals; rear courtyard for the private conversation.
Ledger House shrine: Oghma (the printed map label says Torm).

entries.name: Drysa — Overnight Watch (Perception Results)
entries: {@b Drysa:} Austin rolls d20 + 5, Wisdom (Perception). Passive Perception 15; Stealth +4; Darkvision 60 ft.; Blindsight 10 ft. Base report plus each achieved tier.

{@b Any total:} 'Drysa observed the southern public entrance and the western loading entrance used for deliveries. The building became quieter after business hours. Most production lights went dark, but a light remained in the southern part of the building late into the night. Neither entrance had a guard permanently stationed outside during the periods she watched.'

{@b Total 15+:} 'A large, heavily built figure carrying a weapon crossed the western loading approach, disappeared into the building, and later returned. It appeared to be patrolling.' From close enough and with enough light, she identifies the figure as a Bugbear.
{@b Total 20+:} 'It returned to the loading approach roughly every eight minutes. A short interval after it disappeared inside appeared particularly promising for reaching that entrance.'

{@b Total 25+:} 'Across the patrol cycles she watched, no other guard took its place outside. She observed a short interval when nobody outside had a direct view of the western entrance. That doesn't tell her who might be watching from inside.'

{@b Limits:} The report covers the exterior only. For distant observations, Drysa returns to Aaron before communicating outside familiar range. Closer scouting: Stealth +4 if detection is possible. Additional deductions from actual clues: Intelligence (Investigation), suggested DC 13.

entries.name: Detritus — Arrival
entries: Detritus (Elena) is a male Rock Gnome Wizard 4. A vision showed that his home is in danger of destruction; he's searching for a way to prevent it. His home's location, exact vision, cause and timing have not been established.
Detritus arrives at Ledger House seeking local information. Marren Library is a potential research destination Brakkus can identify. Elena describes Detritus's appearance and introduction.
{@b Brakkus:} 'These folks have seen a fair bit of Bellweather lately. They may be able to point you in the right direction.'

entries.name: Brakkus and Aaron — Private Conversation
entries: Brakkus invites Aaron to the rear courtyard. He knows Aaron is a dhampir; details about Dimidicus, Aaron's dreams and the mysterious liberator are not known to him unless Aaron shares them.
{@b Opening:} 'Aaron, can I ask you something? What brought you to Bellweather? How did you find your way to my door?'

{@b If Aaron mentions the pull toward Bellweather or Ledger House:} 'I serve Oghma. I've wondered whether he had a hand in your finding this place. That's all it is, though: a suspicion. I don't have an answer.'

{@b If Aaron raises his dhampir nature:} 'I know. It hasn't changed your welcome here.' If asked why: 'My father was a warlord. My mother was a librarian he kept captive. She taught me to read.' Brakkus's mother Elena taught him to seek knowledge and respect people beyond their ancestry.

{@b If Aaron discusses his former master:} Brakkus offers to help him find reliable information. He has no identified answer about Aaron's liberator. If Aaron ends the conversation: 'Fair enough. My door's open if you change your mind.'

entries.name: Jord — A Room and a Gift
entries: Jord, the 86-year-old gnome trader with sandy hair, spectacles and an overstuffed patched coat, arrives at Ledger House carrying his luggage. The Royal Guard has requisitioned his hotel for barracks. He asks Brakkus for a room. He recognizes the adventurers who recovered his stolen horse and strongbox.
{@b Gift:} Jord offers his personal {@item Hat of Disguise|XDMG} to the party permanently. 'You saved my horse and my strongbox. Reckon you can get better use out of this than I have. Here, take it.'

{@b Hat of Disguise:} Uncommon; requires attunement (Short Rest). Attuned wearer casts {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} at will; each casting lasts 1 hour and ends if the hat is removed. Transfer when accepted in play.
{@b Trade:} Jord's 20% discount remains in force. The gifted hat was his personal possession and does not change either merchant's shop inventory.

images.title: Koven House — Original DM Key (Conditional Fight)

entries.name: Session 4 — PLAYED / Authoritative
entries: After the Well, the party killed Noren and his Veteran. The Veteran was beheaded; Arunem carried the body in a bag. A city guard confirmed the Council was gone. The bag was repeatedly slammed to the ground; the precise actor and final whereabouts of the body are not recorded.
Pepper went alone to the market and had a bad encounter with Edda Pell, half-orc owner of The Spare Button, now voiced with an Irish accent.

Pepper voluntarily approached Koven House to report Edda. Royal guards recognized her in their records, asserted the Crown held her service contract and detained her for hard labor at the southern ruins.
Brakkus found and accompanied Jarrock and Aaron in seeking Pepper. He persuaded the guards to release Pepper into HIS custody. This was a negotiated release; exact custody terms remain unresolved.

Bishop Brann told the party the Council sold Bellweather and departed; Brann did not take a payment from the Crown's acquisition. He proposed covert intelligence sharing while the group appeared to be cooperative Crown hires.
Brann paid outstanding Kellan's Well wages: Jarrock RECEIVED 100 gp, Aaron RECEIVED 100 gp, Arunem RECEIVED 100 gp, Pepper RECEIVED nothing. These payments are already complete.
Brakkus described an old legend of possible mind-affecting magic in Bellweather. Only the legend was shared; the Well's identity and position remain unknown to Brakkus.
Tulcornix Avemvir, Kaleb's adopted aarakocra brother, sought help freeing his sister-in-law Elowen, Kaleb's widow, from Crown-controlled Weavehouse indenture.
At the table Elowen's alleged debt was stated as 150 gp principal, 200 gp administrative charges and 50 gp/day for room and board. Pepper offered all her money. No release or payment is confirmed.
Aaron stationed Drysa to watch the Weavehouse overnight. The party started planning a covert rescue; Brakkus advised stealth.

entries.name: Crown Knowledge — DM Reference
entries: King Hendrix Stucky reigns; Prince Reginald and Princess Narcia administer Bellweather. The former Council, including Perrin Cardon, has departed.
Koven House accepts public petitions and administers Crown contracts. Brakkus negotiated Pepper's release into his custody, with the precise conditions still unresolved.
The Radiant Well is a real magical phenomenon below Bellweather (DM knowledge). Brakkus and the party know only an old legend; its location, workings and the Crown's involvement remain unestablished.
The Crown has no known connection between Tulcornix and the adventurers.

entries.name: Location Only — OPEN
entries: Savin Keep and its established location and maps remain available. Old reclamation orders, faction assignments, soldiers, treasure and outcomes have been retired.
Rebuild new events later from the Crown-era world and the party's choices.

entries.name: RUN SHEET — 2024 Initiative, Monsters and Security
entries: PRIVATE SUITE: Jaroood, Earth Elemental, Gargoyle and Mimic (281 HP total, 2,725 XP). LABOR SECURITY: Captain at Room 11, Warrior at Rooms 9/10, Bugbear on western/southern patrol. Stat blocks below.

entries.caption: Room 19 — Private fight
rows: Rapier +3, 1d8+1 (avg 5) piercing. Misty Step and Detect Magic 1/LR each; Prestidigitation at will; spell DC 13. Speaks Common/Elvish/Terran.

2 attacks in any mix: Slam +8, 10-ft reach, 2d8+5 (avg 14) bludgeoning; Rock Launch +8, 60 ft., 1d6+5 (avg 8) bludgeoning and Prone (Large or smaller). Tremorsense 60 ft.; vulnerable to Thunder; Siege Monster (double vs objects/structures); Earth Glide only through unworked earth/stone.
Multiattack 2 Claws, +4, 2d4+2 (avg 7) slashing each; Fly 60 ft., Flyby avoids opportunity attacks when flying out of reach. Room 19 ceiling 15 ft.

Pseudopod +5: 1d8+3 bludgeoning +1d8 acid (avg 11), Grapple DC 13 against Large/smaller, escape ability checks with Disadvantage. Bite +5: normal 1d8+3 piercing +1d8 acid (avg 11); against Grappled target, 2d8+3 piercing +1d8 acid (avg 16), attack with Advantage. Bonus action Shape-Shift; immune to Acid and Prone.

entries: SENSES: Jaroood passive Perception 14; Earth Elemental 10 (Tremorsense 60 ft.); Gargoyle 10 (Stealth +4); Mimic 11 (Stealth +5); Captain 10; Warrior 10; Bugbear 10 (Stealth +6). SPEED: Earth Elemental 30 ft./Burrow 30 ft., Gargoyle 30 ft./Fly 60 ft., Mimic 20 ft., all three labor guards 30 ft.
STARTING POSITIONS: Jaroood at the desk and bell pull, Elowen attending him; Gargoyle among the stonework; Mimic as a gilded document coffer; Earth Elemental in Room 19 after the shift.

CIVILIANS: Clerk, Elowen and ordinary workers use {@creature Commoner|XMM}: initiative +0 (10), AC 10, HP 4, Speed 30 ft., Passive Perception 10. In an escape they seek cover or flee. 2024 nonlethal melee: a target otherwise reduced to 0 HP can be left Unconscious at 1 HP.

ELEMENTAL TRIGGER: mere Tremorsense movement is NOT hostile action. It attacks upon deliberate Terran order from Jaroood or perceiving actual attacks/effects upon Jaroood or itself. The attacker may be unseen, but the attack must actually be perceived. Mimic reacts to being handled/seeing prey or a genuine fight; does not obey spoken orders. Gargoyle protects Jaroood when ordered or threatened.
JAROOOD: AC 15, HP 9. He may give a Terran defense command, sound the internal bell, use Misty Step, bargain, flee or surrender.

entries.caption: Labor guards — secondary fight only if genuinely encountered
rows: 2 Greatsword +4, 2d6+2 slashing +1d6 poison (avg 12) EACH, or 2 Longbow +4, 1d8+2 piercing +2d4 poison (avg 11) each. Aura of Authority: self and allies within 10 ft. gain Advantage on attacks and saves while Captain not Incapacitated.
Longsword +3, 2d10+1 (avg 12) slashing; Longbow +3, 1d8+1 piercing +3d4 poison (avg 12) damage. Pack Tactics: Advantage on attack if ally within 5 ft. of target and not Incapacitated.

Grab +4, 10-ft reach, 2d6+2 (avg 9) bludgeoning + Grappled (Medium/smaller, escape DC12); Light Hammer +4, 10-ft reach or 20/60 ft., 3d4+2 (avg 9) bludgeoning, Advantage if target grappled by Bugbear. Abduct: moves grappled creature without extra movement.

entries: CREATURE TYPE: Hobgoblin Captain, Hobgoblin Warrior and Bugbear Warrior are Fey (Goblinoid) under 2024 rules. Hold Person requires a Humanoid.

GUARDS: One unexplained noise → one investigator ('Must be the wind' if nothing found). Sustained fighting → investigation and report. Alarm/breakout → Captain directs containment, Warrior secures doors, Bugbear captures escaping workers alive.

LOCKS & EXIT: West loading/service lock DC 15 Thieves' Tools after hours. Exposed cord outside Room 19: quietly detach DC 13 Thieves' Tools or cut with an action (AC 12, HP 5). Worker doors Rooms 9 (4 people), 10 (4), 17 (5), 18 (4) open with Jaroood master key ONE ACTION EACH; otherwise DC 15 Thieves' Tools. Workers bolt independently toward existing Room 21 western or Room 23 southern access, no escort or pooled Stealth rolls.

MINIS: Earth Elemental #151 (p.19 back bottom left); Gargoyle #121 (p.16 front top left); Mimic #115 (p.15 front bottom left); Hobgoblin Captain #72 (p.9 back bottom right); Hobgoblin Warrior #59 (p.8 front bottom left); Bugbear Warrior #70 (p.9 back top right); Jaroood proxy #28 (p.4 front bottom right).

STAT LINKS: {@creature Earth Elemental|XMM}, {@creature Gargoyle|XMM}, {@creature Mimic|XMM}, {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM}, {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM}, {@creature Bugbear Warrior|XMM}, {@creature Jaroood|NCFA}.
HAT OF DISGUISE (if accepted and attuned): {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} at will, one hour, ends on removal. Inspect illusion: Study action, Intelligence (Investigation) vs the wearer's spell save DC.

entries.name: Routes — Approaches, Patrols and Escape
entries: SOUTH: Room 23 public approach → southern hall → existing corridor on the west of Room 19 → suite doorway.
WEST: Room 21 loading access → western service aisle past Room 8 → worker-wing corridor near Rooms 17/18 → southern hall → west-side doorway of Room 19.

BUGBEAR: Room 21 loading threshold → service corridor past Room 8 → passage outside Rooms 9/10 → southern passage outside Rooms 17/18 → return along the same route to Room 21. Approximately 8 minutes including checks.

WARRIOR: Corridor post outside Rooms 9/10 → hourly inspection at the approaches to Rooms 17/18 → return. CAPTAIN: Room 11 → existing central passage bordering Room 15 → south passage toward west-side access of Room 19 when an actual response is warranted.

WORKERS: Rooms 9/10 may reach western loading Room 21 or turn south toward Room 23; Rooms 17/18 may reach southern access Room 23 or the west loading route via Room 21. Guards intercept by physical position and movement.
Map scale: 10 feet. During initiative, use measured distances for guards and Large creatures.

entries.name: The Map — All 25 Numbered Rooms
entries: Numbered locations on the approved Weavehouse map:
1. Timekeeper and attendance desk: Daytime clerk checks work hours and labor slips.
2. Public receiving/check-in: Petitions and escorted visitors are directed from here.
3. Wool inspection: Raw fleece is counted and graded.
4. North weaving floor: Active looms by day, empty production area overnight.
5. Thread and dye ingredients: Locked consumable store.
6. Finished cloth inventory: Counted bales awaiting dispatch.
7. North store closet: Routine tools and wrapping supplies.
8. Western service passage: Bugbear patrol waypoint.
9. Worker sleeping room A: Four workers; locked after headcount.
10. Worker sleeping room B: Four workers; locked after headcount.
11. Chief overseer's office: Hobgoblin Captain's desk, central roster, spare worker keys, reporting bell.
12. Clerk files and supplies: Routine records and work orders.
13. Dyeing/pressing workroom: Workers during day, generally quiet at night.
14. Eastern service passage: Circulation to rooms on the east side.
15. Main production hall: Large work floor and loom machinery; Earth Elemental stationed here during the day.
16. Cloth finishing and packing: Packed stock, bales and ordinary supplies.
17. Worker sleeping room C: Five workers; locked after headcount.
18. Worker sleeping room D: Four workers; locked after headcount.
19. Jaroood's private office and quarters: Jaroood and Elowen; Gargoyle, Mimic and nighttime Earth Elemental.
20. Jaroood's private secure filing room: Account records, release paperwork and correspondence.
21. Western receiving/loading point: Service entrance and western exit.
22. Raw-material storage: Cotton and wool bundles.
23. South public approach and reception: Visitor access and front-facing circulation.
24. Dispatch/staging: Outgoing cloth and bundles.
25. Eastern storage and housekeeping: Cleaning and service supplies.

entries.name: Workers, Guard Posts and Daily Schedule
entries: 18 indentured workers in total: Room 9: four; Room 10: four; Room 17: five; Room 18: four; Elowen in Room 19. The dormitories are locked after evening headcount.
CAPTAIN: {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM}, Room 11, with roster, keys and alarm bell. Coordinates responses to breakouts.
WARRIOR: {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM} posted in the corridor outside Rooms 9/10, carrying room keys. Checks the corridor outside Rooms 17/18 once an hour, then returns along the same passages.

BUGBEAR: {@creature Bugbear Warrior|XMM} checks the Room 21 loading threshold, passes the Room 8 corridor and workers' approach corridors near Rooms 9/10 and 17/18, then returns. An eight-minute circuit includes inspections and pauses. Investigates a lone sound before resuming his circuit.
CLERK: works near Rooms 2 and 11 during business hours and leaves after closing. Jaroood handles inspections and petitions by day; he and Elowen remain in Room 19 overnight.
PERSONAL DEFENDERS: {@creature Earth Elemental|XMM}, Room 15 by day and 19 after close; {@creature Gargoyle|XMM}, stone decoration in 19; {@creature Mimic|XMM}, gilded coffer in 19.

entries.name: Access, Alarm, Doors and Security Response
entries: ENTRANCES: Public entry at Room 23; Room 21 loading access locked after hours (DC 15 Dexterity [Thieves' Tools]). The Bugbear passes Room 21 on patrol. Drysa's exterior report is in Chapter 6.

BELL: Room 19 pull cord reaches a brass bell at Room 11 through ceiling/wall eyelets. A reachable segment outside Room 19 can be quietly disconnected with DC 13 Dexterity (Thieves' Tools) or cut as an action (AC 12, 5 HP). The bell alerts only people inside the Weavehouse.

NOISE: One ambiguous sound → one guard investigates, then 'Must be the wind' if no evidence. Sustained fighting, broken doors or escaping workers → continued investigation and ordinary report to the Captain.

ALARM / BREAKOUT: Captain coordinates from Room 11, Warrior secures locked quarters, Bugbear recaptures escapees. Guards use grapples, shoves, restraints and nonlethal melee on workers; armed intruders may be attacked lethally.

KEYS: Master key on Jaroood opens all four worker rooms; Warrior and Captain have keys. Each door costs one action to unlock and open with a key. Picking a lock is DC 15 Dexterity (Thieves' Tools). Workers run independently as soon as their own door opens.

EARTH ELEMENTAL: 60-ft Tremorsense detects contact with a connected surface, not a creature's identity or intention. It activates on Jaroood's explicit Terran command 'Defend your master' OR when it actually perceives an attack affecting Jaroood or itself in Room 19; it need not see the attacker. Mere footsteps never trigger combat.

OTHER DEFENDERS: Gargoyle reacts to a clear attack or Terran order. Mimic responds to disturbance, prey or fighting in its area, not verbal orders. Earth Glide does not let the Earth Elemental pass through worked stone walls.

entries.name: Authority and Elowen
entries: Cardon Weavehouse belongs to the Crown. Perrin Cardon departed with the former Council. Jaroood has complete operational authority over the workers, production, discipline, fees and release orders.

Jaroood is a 243-year-old high elf who arrived with Prince Reginald. He profits from the forced labor system through 10% of new debt assessed beyond each worker's original principal. His priority is wealth and his standing with the Crown.

Elowen, Kaleb's widow, serves Jaroood and wants freedom. The party heard 150 gp principal + 200 gp administrative charges + 50 gp per billed day; Jaroood's current ledger shows four billed days (550 gp total), not yet disclosed to the party. Pepper offered money, with no payment confirmed.

entries.name: Jaroood — Appearance, Answers and Decisions
entries: {@b First description (read or paraphrase).} A slender high elf in a perfectly fitted burgundy coat stands behind a desk. His silver-blond hair is combed straight back from a narrow face; pale-gold eyes pass over you with brisk calculation. A heavy gold signet of the Crown sits on one long finger. He speaks in a refined, slightly nasal voice that makes even an insult sound like a courtesy.

{@b Voice and gestures.} Perform a younger and more vigorous Mr. Burns: nasal, soft, precise, delighted by profit, and condescending without shouting. He steeples his fingers when pleased, checks the edge of a ledger before replying, glances at a pocket watch when someone wastes time, and uses {@spell Prestidigitation|XPHB} to clean dust from his clothes after inspections. When royal authority is credible, he straightens and becomes swiftly deferential.

{@b Belief and motivation:} He regards indentured slavery as justified debt collection and workers as sources of profit. He wants wealth, security and continuing royal favor. He fears the Crown's displeasure.
{@b Authority:} Jaroood controls operations, assessments, custody and discharge signatures at the Crown-owned Weavehouse. He can sign Elowen's release himself; authentic royal orders outrank him.

{@b Elowen's account:} Four billed days: 150 gp principal + 200 gp administrative fees + 200 gp board = {@b 550 gp}. Jaroood's authorized commission on the added charges: {@b 40 gp}. Every additional billed day adds 50 gp to the balance and 5 gp to his commission.

{@b Routine:} Morning work orders and inspections; afternoon petitions and fees; evening accounting in Room 19, his private residential suite. Elowen serves and sleeps behind a screen in Room 19. Jaroood's private files are in Room 20; the labor ledger is held with the clerical records by Room 11.
{@b Possessions:} Crown signet ring, gold watch, personal commission ledger and master key for all four sleeping rooms (9, 10, 17, 18).
{@b Knows:} Names and debt accounts of workers, internal security, authorized Crown procedures. He has no knowledge of Tulcornix having approached the PCs or of their covert plan.

{@b Talk and bargain:} He quotes the account on the day of inquiry. Full payment or a valid order can produce a signed release. Deception about royal credentials: suggested DC 15 Charisma (Deception) when a check is warranted, with circumstances affecting difficulty. His commission is legal, not incriminating leverage.

{@b Under attack:} AC 15, 9 HP. Jaroood can pull the bell in Room 19, command the Gargoyle and Earth Elemental in Primordial (Terran), use {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} once per Long Rest, negotiate, surrender or run. See {@creature Jaroood|NCFA}.

{@b Suggested lines.} 'Slavery? No, no. A structured opportunity to settle one's obligations.' / 'You cannot expect accommodations to pay for themselves.' / 'How gratifying. Another account adjusted upward.' / 'His Highness has ordered it? Naturally, that changes everything.'

entries.name: Room 19 — Confrontation and Elowen
entries: {@b Scene:} Jaroood is working at his desk with Elowen attending to papers. The suite's ceiling is 15 feet high. A screened cot stands nearby. The Gargoyle looks like stone decoration, the Mimic like a decorated document chest, and the Earth Elemental is present after hours.
{@b Elowen:} She seeks cover or a way out if fighting starts. She knows Kaleb is dead. Whether she knows Pepper killed him is not established. Opening line: 'Who are you? What are you doing here?'
{@b Combatants:} Jaroood 9 HP, Earth Elemental 147, Gargoyle 67, Mimic 58. The labor guards begin at their ordinary posts and respond to any alarm or evidence they receive.

{@b Defenders:} Jaroood can pull the bell or command his defenders in Terran. The Earth Elemental reacts to a command or an attack it perceives; Gargoyle to threats/orders; Mimic to nearby prey/violence.

entries.name: Release, Escape and Investigation
entries: Once a worker-room door opens, its occupants run toward accessible exterior doors on their own: Room 9 (4), 10 (4), 17 (5), 18 (4). Elowen is the eighteenth. Guards may catch individuals but are forbidden to kill worker assets.
An early breakout alerts any guard who discovers it. Jaroood can respond if he receives a warning; guards unaware of a confrontation remain on their assigned duties.

The Crown investigates discovered murders, property destruction and escapes through staff testimony, physical evidence and accounts. It currently has no knowledge linking the party and Tulcornix. Outstanding debt claims persist after an unauthorized physical escape.

entries.name: Current State
entries: Next is Session 5, four level-4 PCs: Jarrock, Aaron Dunamus, Arunem and Pepper. The primary open activity is Elowen's rescue from the Crown's Weavehouse.
Noren and his Veteran are dead. The Council and Cardon are gone. Brann paid the 300 gp owed to Jarrock, Aaron and Arunem. Pepper is under Brakkus's negotiated custody after Crown detention.
Brakkus follows Oghma and knows Aaron is a dhampir; he plans a conversation. Aaron's familiar is watching the Weavehouse, but has reported no established findings.
The Crown owns the Weavehouse; Jaroood is its greedy administrator. Future chapters keep places, not old plots.

entries.name: Explicitly OPEN
entries: Elowen's actual rescue, Jaroood's specific methods and daily schedule, surveillance findings, exact custody papers for Pepper, the Crown's knowledge of the party's intentions, and details of the developing resistance.
The Radiant Well's true mechanism, access, relation to future sites and any Crown knowledge or motive.
The party's eventual relationship with the Stucky monarchy and all future chapter events.
Character destinies and unresolved backstories unless the players establish them.

entries.name: Brakkus Ledgerhelm
entries: About 48, half-orc, level-16 Oath of Devotion paladin of Oghma. Retired by choice, proprietor of Ledger House, protective of people in his care.

Father: Korgak, Ironfang warlord. Mother: Elena, a captive human librarian who taught Brakkus literacy, knowledge and human dignity. After her death he rejected his father's legacy and took the surname Ledgerhelm.
Mentor: High Justiciar Vance Halford. Vance gave him the magic sword Brakkus named The Appendix.
Brakkus's faith was Oghma when played at Hall of Heroes, and remains Oghma in NCFA. He knows Aaron is a dhampir and seeks to understand him.
He negotiated Pepper's release into custody and is a credible independent civic actor. He is not a required field companion or solution to player obstacles.

For Session 5, privately ask Aaron what drew him to Bellweather and Ledger House. Brakkus knows he's dhampir but has no confirmed knowledge of his liberator or divine intervention. His possible Oghma role is speculation, not fact.

entries.name: Royal Administration
entries: King Hendrix Stucky reigns from outside Bellweather. Prince Reginald Stucky governs with his wife Princess Narcia Stucky. Their choices have consequences even if their manners are ridiculous.

Jaroood is a 243-year-old HIGH ELF and the Crown's absolute operational administrator at Cardon Weavehouse. He accompanied Prince Reginald to Bellweather, believes debt slavery justified and profits from it through a 10% Crown-approved commission on additional debts ASSESSED against each worker beyond original principal. His authority covers personnel, work, discipline, fee assessment and discharges. He fears losing Crown favor, not the workers' suffering. His young-Mr.-Burns voice is refined, nasal and condescending. He has pale-gold eyes, silver-blond hair and immaculate burgundy and ivory dress.
Perrin Cardon departed with the former Council and has no continuing ownership of the Weavehouse.

243-year-old high elf, 5 ft. 11 in., slender, pale gold eyes, silver-blond slicked-back hair, burgundy coat, ivory waistcoat and Crown signet. Younger, more vigorous Mr. Burns voice; steeples fingers and uses Prestidigitation to clean lint after inspections.

He controls personnel, discipline, assignments, assessments, and releases at the Crown-owned Weavehouse. He receives a Crown-authorized 10% commission on debt ADDED beyond original principal for every worker, credited as assessed, not based on actual repayment. Elowen's stated 200 gp fee yields him 20 gp; every 50 gp/day charge yields 5 gp per day. No days assumed.
High elf magic and combat stats are in {@creature Jaroood|NCFA}. He is an administrator, and his commission is not illicit from the Crown's viewpoint; disclosing it alone cannot blackmail him.

entries.name: Bishop Brann, Tulcornix and Elowen
entries: Brann stayed, refused a payout from the city's sale, paid the remaining Well wages, and is helping coordinate an emerging quiet resistance with Brakkus.
Tulcornix Avemvir is Kaleb's adopted aarakocra brother, who sought Pepper because she killed Kaleb and requested help rescuing his sister-in-law Elowen.
Elowen is Kaleb's widow and a Crown-confined textile worker. Her stated debt is in Chapter 8, and her future is not predetermined.

entries.name: Player Character Threads
entries: Aaron: dhampir; prior domination by Dimidicus is his personal history, not evidence of a royal or Well conspiracy. The implied Oghma involvement is a question.
Pepper: cleric; old Council penance, current negotiated Crown custody with Brakkus, unresolved relationship to Kaleb's family.
Jarrock: had reported Pepper's killing of Kaleb; drinks despite objections, and his personal trajectory toward confronting royal abuse must arise through play rather than a scripted destiny.
Arunem: described appearing in Bellweather after previously being at home; mechanism unexplained.

Detritus (Elena): male Rock Gnome Wizard 4; has seen a vision of his home's destruction and is trying to PREVENT it. Home, origin/cause/time/detail of vision and wizard subclass/spells OPEN. Introduce him at Ledger House. Possible Marren Library research does not establish a plot connection.
Drysa: Aaron's pseudodragon familiar. Overnight exterior surveillance opening is ONE Wisdom (Perception) d20+5 with cumulative 15/20/25 tiers, in Chapter 6; no results played yet.

data.name: Appendix G: Generic DM Quick Reference

entries.name: Generic DCs
entries: Use these values when the adventure does not specify a DC. Choose the ability and skill from the character's approach. If success is automatic or impossible, do not call for a roll.

entries.name: Object and Material ACs and HP
entries: Use AC to determine whether an attack damages an unattended object. HP represents how much punishment the object can take before it breaks. In the core object rules, material primarily determines AC while size and whether the construction is fragile or resilient determine HP; the values below combine those rules into a fast DM reference.

The HP columns assume a typical fragile build for cloth/paper/rope and crystal/glass/ice, and a typical resilient build for wood/bone, stone, metal, mithral, and adamantine. Use a lower HP category for thin, rotten, cracked, or poorly made objects and a higher one for unusually thick or reinforced construction. For walls, gates, vehicles, and other very large structures, treat the attacked portion as a separate object and consider a damage threshold when appropriate.

entries.caption: Object AC and Typical HP by Material
Object HP by Size and Construction
Light and Obscurement
rows: Lightly Obscured; Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
Heavily Obscured; a creature effectively has the Blinded condition when trying to see into it.
Within its range, treat Dim Light as Bright Light and Darkness as Dim Light; colors in Darkness appear only as shades of gray.
Within its range, perceive without normal sight, including through Darkness and against Invisible creatures, unless blocked by Total Cover.
Within its range, see through normal and magical Darkness, see Invisible creatures, and automatically pierce visual illusions as specified by the sense.

entries.caption: Common Condition Summary
rows: Can't see; automatically fails sight-dependent checks; attacks against the creature have Advantage, and its attacks have Disadvantage.
Can't attack the charmer or target it with harmful effects; the charmer has Advantage on social checks involving the creature.
Can't hear and automatically fails checks that require hearing.
Disadvantage on ability checks and attacks while the source is in line of sight; can't willingly move closer to the source.
Speed 0; Disadvantage on attacks against targets other than the grappler; the grappler can move the creature with extra movement cost in most cases.
Can't take actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions; Concentration ends; can't speak; Initiative is rolled with Disadvantage if already Incapacitated.
Normally can't be targeted by effects requiring sight; Advantage on own attacks and Disadvantage on attacks against it unless the attacker can see it; Advantage on Initiative.
Incapacitated; Speed 0; automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves; attacks against it have Advantage; qualifying close-range hits can become critical hits.
Incapacitated; Speed 0; attacks against it have Advantage; automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves; Resistance to all damage and immunity to Poisoned.
Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
Crawl or spend half Speed to stand; own attacks have Disadvantage; attacks from within 5 feet have Advantage, otherwise attacks have Disadvantage.
Speed 0; attacks against the creature have Advantage; its attacks have Disadvantage; Disadvantage on Dexterity saves.
Incapacitated; Speed 0; automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves; attacks against it have Advantage.
Incapacitated and Prone; drops held items; Speed 0; attacks against it have Advantage; automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves; qualifying close-range hits can become critical hits.

entries.name: Falling
entries: A creature takes 1d6 Bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet fallen, to a maximum of 20d6, and lands Prone unless an effect says otherwise.

entries.name: Jumping

entries.caption: Jumping Quick Reference
rows: Up to Strength score in feet

entries: Each foot jumped costs 1 foot of movement. Landing in Difficult Terrain after a Long Jump requires a DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or the jumper becomes Prone. At the DM's option, clearing a low obstacle during a Long Jump can require a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check. A creature can reach upward an additional distance equal to half its height during a High Jump.

items: {@b Use common sense.} An attack that cannot reasonably damage an object deals no meaningful damage regardless of the attack roll.

{@b Damage Threshold.} If an object has a damage threshold, damage from a single attack or effect below that threshold deals 0 damage; meeting or exceeding the threshold allows the full damage through.
{@b Damage Types.} Objects are generally immune to Poison and Psychic damage. Assign additional resistances, vulnerabilities, or immunities when the material makes them obvious.
{@b Huge and Gargantuan Objects.} Divide very large structures into Large or smaller sections and track damage to the relevant section rather than treating an entire building as one object.
{@b Automatic Breakage.} If an object is extremely fragile and the method is appropriate, allow it to be broken without rolling.

entries.name: Improvised Damage
entries: Use this when the environment causes damage and no specific rule gives a value. Choose the damage amount that best matches the severity of the event rather than the source's physical size alone.

entries.caption: Improvised Damage Examples
rows: Minor but meaningful hazard, such as hot coals or a heavy object falling onto someone.
Serious hazard, such as a lightning strike or falling into a firepit.
Severe hazard, such as collapsing rubble or falling into a vat of acid.
Extreme hazard, such as crushing machinery or moving through lava.
Catastrophic hazard, such as being submerged in lava or struck by a massive crashing structure.
Near-apocalyptic force appropriate to exceptionally destructive supernatural or colossal events.

entries.name: Common Improvised DC Examples
entries: These are generic examples, not fixed DCs. Adjust for tools, leverage, time pressure, conditions, and the character's approach.

entries.caption: Improvised DC Examples
rows: Climb a knotted rope with good footing; notice something obvious while actively searching.
Force a weak interior door; climb a rough wall with ample handholds; calm a mildly agitated animal.
Pick an ordinary lock; climb a wet or awkward surface; spot a reasonably concealed compartment; recall specialized lore.
Force a reinforced door; detect a carefully hidden feature; perform a difficult physical maneuver under pressure.
Defeat exceptional mundane security; accomplish a feat demanding rare expertise or strength.
Accomplish a legendary but still physically possible feat without magical assistance.

entries.name: Exhaustion
entries: Exhaustion is cumulative from level 1 through 6. A creature dies when it reaches Exhaustion level 6. Finishing a Long Rest normally removes 1 Exhaustion level.

entries.caption: Common Environmental Hazards
rows: A burning creature or object takes 1d4 Fire damage at the start of each turn until the fire is extinguished, doused, submerged, or suffocated.
At 0°F or below, make a DC 10 Constitution save each hour or gain 1 Exhaustion level. Cold Resistance or Immunity automatically succeeds.

At 100°F or above without drinkable water, make an hourly Constitution save: DC 5 for the first hour, +1 per additional hour. Medium/Heavy armor gives Disadvantage; Fire Resistance or Immunity automatically succeeds.

After a number of minutes equal to Constitution score, make a DC 10 Constitution save each additional minute or gain 1 Exhaustion level. Cold Resistance/Immunity or natural adaptation automatically succeeds.
After each hour swimming deeper than 100 feet, a creature without a Swim Speed makes a DC 10 Constitution save or gains 1 Exhaustion level.
Difficult Terrain; entering it for the first time on a turn or starting there requires a DC 10 Dexterity save or the creature becomes Prone.
Disadvantage on ranged weapon attacks; extinguishes open flames and disperses fog; flying creatures generally must land by the end of their turn or fall.
Area is Lightly Obscured and sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks have Disadvantage; heavy rain also extinguishes open flames.
Use the Improvised Damage table when no specific acid effect applies; a severe immersion or vat-level exposure is typically represented by the higher damage entries.
Use the Improvised Damage table: moving through lava is an extreme hazard; full submersion is catastrophic.

entries.name: 15 NPC Names
entries: Use these for incidental NPCs when a name is needed immediately. Assign ancestry, occupation, and personality to fit the scene.

data.name: Appendix J: Bellwether Shops and Inventories
entries: DM inventory reference for Bellwether. These inventories begin after the party's Kellan's Well expedition and are independent of the PCs' level, needs, and available gold. Prices use the normal-price column of the D&D Shop Catalog V2.0.2 (Refresh) where applicable; invented curiosities have DM-set prices. GP = gold, SP = silver, CP = copper. Quantities are physical stock at this snapshot, not permanent supply guarantees.

Sale procedure: quote the displayed price, decrease stock on sale, keep sold items sold until a believable resupply occurs. Goods not listed here can be ordered or searched for in the city if appropriate; this inventory is the merchant's opening stock, not a prohibition on the existence of other merchandise in the world. 'One crate/box/set' means one indivisible lot unless the merchant agrees to split it.

Magic pricing reference from the catalog: Common 100 gp, Uncommon 400 gp, Rare 4,000 gp, Very Rare 40,000 gp, Legendary 200,000 gp. The catalog prices spell scrolls by level separately (cantrip 50 gp; level 1 100 gp; level 2 250 gp; level 3 500 gp; level 4 2,500 gp; level 5 5,000 gp). Individual consumables below use their listed prices. Rarity prices are campaign shop prices, not guarantees of availability.
Merchants have independent businesses, lives and motives. Not every inventory entry is a clue.

entries.name: Selling Loot and Trading Equipment — Session 4
entries: {@b 2024 PHB equipment resale.} Usable ordinary equipment sells for HALF its listed purchase cost. Trade goods and valuables (such as gems and art objects) retain their face value. Apply only to items the party actually collected, kept and brings to a willing buyer; undiscovered gear cannot be sold.

{@b At the table.} Joren Viton of the Two Hammers is the natural buyer for serviceable arms and armor, with Maten inspecting condition when needed. Standard examples at their listed shop prices: a 50 gp greatsword sells for 25 gp, a 50 gp longbow sells for 25 gp, a 50 gp heavy crossbow sells for 25 gp, a 10 gp shortsword sells for 5 gp, and a 50 gp chain shirt sells for 25 gp. These are resale values, not extra encounter treasure. A merchant need not accept unsafe, counterfeit or unusable gear.

{@b Well ledger distinction.} The site contains 375 gp in fixed money/valuables, including 75 gp of salvage valuables. The valuables portion is already counted at its face value; DO NOT half it again or count it twice. The Well's confiscated weapons are separate physical gear that may have resale value if the party actually kept them. Don't automatically credit the party every weapon from every defeated defender.

{@b Magic and unusual property.} Magic item purchase costs follow the established campaign shop catalog. Do not infer a guaranteed half-price magic buyback from the ordinary-equipment rule; buyers can quote a price for a specific item. Keep each merchant's stock persistent, honor Jord's party discount when buying from him, and record actual completed sales.

entries.name: The Tiny Mage — Tiera Dame
entries: General store in the Slums. Despite its name, it sells everyday merchandise rather than magic. Tiera Dame is a 48-year-old halfling woman, small even by halfling standards, with curly auburn hair, dark-brown eyes, a green vest under her practical apron, and keys and small pouches at her belt. She is friendly, quick-speaking, observant, slightly gossipy, and suspicious of people who watch the shelves more than the price tags. She sorts stock while speaking. Her attention to local comings and goings makes her a useful neighbor, not a professional informant. Pepper met her during Session 1, when she warned about thieves in the Slums.
Portrayal cue: "Want fifty feet of rope? Had somebody buy three hundred feet last week. Never did find out why. Anyway, one gold."

entries.name: The Tiny Mage: Odd Warehouse Lot

entries.caption: The Tiny Mage: Odd Warehouse Lot
rows: Taxidermied goose in a removable judge's wig
Crate of 73 assorted LEFT boots, no right boots
Box of 400 one-inch carved wooden ducks
Brass ship's bell missing its clapper
Wedding cake topper depicting two ogres
Portrait of an unidentified man labeled 'Gerald'
Enormous brass key, unknown matching lock

entries: Odd-lot policy: Tiera bought a warehouse lot cheaply. She does not know why these objects were manufactured and has no special reason to think they are enchanted, cursed, prophetic, or related to the main plot. Most are mundane. If the players find clever practical uses for them, adjudicate normally. Some items can sell permanently out and be replaced later by wholly different junk.
If asked why she owns these: "Bought a warehouse lot. Got a good price."

entries.name: The Spare Button — Edda Pell
entries: Arcane merchant and genuine magic shop occupying a former sewing store. Edda Pell is a 54-year-old half-orc woman with short graying hair, round spectacles, rolled-up sleeves, and an apron with more pockets than should be necessary. She is practical, sharply observant, and dry-witted; sells remarkable enchantments as if they were household hardware. She did not replace the old sewing-shop sign because a new sign costs money. The wooden tray of ordinary buttons by the till remains for sale at 3 cp each.
{@b Session 4 table update:} Edda has an Irish accent. Pepper had an unsuccessful merchant encounter with her and reported her at Koven House. The specific repercussions are not yet established.

Portrayal cue: "It flaps. Even indoors. Apparently somebody thought that was worth enchanting." (describing a Cloak of Billowing.) She bargains when given a sensible reason, describes what she knows accurately, and treats nobles and dockworkers alike.

entries.name: The Spare Button: Arcane Materials and Services

entries.caption: The Spare Button: Arcane Materials and Services

entries.name: The Spare Button: Spell Scrolls and Potions

entries.caption: The Spare Button: Spell Scrolls and Potions

entries: Buying magic is ordinary commerce here, not automatically a quest. The costly Ring of Spell Storing is a legitimate for-sale item even if the party cannot afford it. Magic stock is limited and replaced by real acquisitions, not convenience-driven refreshes.

entries.name: The Two Hammers — Joren Viton and Maten
entries: One shared weaponsmith/armorer business, not two separate shops. Joren Viton (human man, 43) is broad-shouldered with a neatly trimmed dark beard beginning to gray and tidy work clothes. Outgoing, commercial, honest, fast-moving, and enthusiastic about ready-stock equipment. He manages sales, prices, ordinary weapons/armor, and special orders. Maten (dwarf man, 112) is a muscular, gray-bearded master smith with thick eyebrows, scarred hands, and a permanently soot-stained apron. Quiet and exacting, he examines a weapon's balance and a client's grip before offering custom work. He is Bellwether's best armorer/weaponsmith. They respect one another: Joren keeps the operation profitable; Maten keeps its reputation.
Joren portrayal cue: "If you need it today, I have exactly what you need." Maten portrayal cue: "Want a sword made for you? Fine. Show me how you hold one."

entries.name: The Two Hammers: Ordinary Weapons and Ammunition

entries.caption: The Two Hammers: Ordinary Weapons and Ammunition

entries: Ordinary Scale Mail is always listed separately from the Mithral Scale Mail. The nonmagical suit provides AC 14 + DEX modifier (maximum +2) and imposes Stealth disadvantage under the game's standard armor rules. Mithral Scale Mail is magical, removes its normal Stealth disadvantage, and otherwise uses the armor's normal AC.

Commissions: custom or specially fitted ordinary gear is approximately +50% of the catalog's normal price and takes 1–3 weeks, according to complexity and workload; Maten can refit armor for different body plans. His superior workmanship does NOT automatically produce +1 attack, damage, or AC. Enchanted inventory above is acquired merchandise; neither smith must be an enchanter. Magical commissions are not automatically available.

entries.name: Jord's Odds & Ends — Jord
entries: Jord is an 86-year-old gnome traveling merchant with sandy, untidy hair, large expressive eyebrows, spectacles sliding down his nose, a patched good-quality coat with too many pockets, broad work-worn shoulders, and the dust of the road about him. Cheerful, quick-talking, resourceful, and a shrewd bargainer; he rummages while he speaks. His wagon carries practical goods, trade-ins, curiosities, and the occasional extraordinary acquisition. The party recovered his stolen strongbox and missing horse; he already rewarded them and promised a discount on future purchases.
Portrayal cue: "I had two, sold one outside the city, and the other might still be—ah! There it is!"

entries.name: Jord: Magic in the Wagon — Opening Snapshot

entries.caption: Jord: Magic in the Wagon — Opening Snapshot
Jord: Oddities and Trade-ins
rows: Barrel of sixty pounds of salt
Locked wooden box, contents unknown to Jord
Pair of boots with mismatched heel heights

entries: Discount continuity, now set for Session 4: after the party recovered his stolen strongbox and missing horse, Jord promised a party discount. The operating rate is 20% off his listed regular asking prices, including listed magic stock; calculate at checkout and decrease stock normally. The discount does not oblige him to buy back items at full retail, or magically replenish stock. If a specific price was already negotiated at the table, honor that prior transaction.

Random acquisition policy: Jord's magical stock is genuinely random and is NEVER capped by the party's current level or funds. He can carry rare, very rare, or legendary items. High-powered acquisitions are saleable at real prices, not automatically restricted to quests. Stock is persistent; items depart when sold, traded, lost, or legitimately moved on. He normally has 2–5 magical entries after a meaningful resupply; reroll only new acquisitions, never his entire existing inventory. The Rare Daern's Instant Fortress in this opening snapshot illustrates that rule.

On each NEW magical acquisition, roll d100 for rarity, then choose or randomly determine an existing magic item of that rarity whose provenance and physical size fit the transaction. Consumables can use their specific catalog prices instead. The table is a stock-generation aid, not permission to replace old stock at every party visit. A result being very rare or legendary does not make it a plot hook. Players may be unable to afford the item until much later.

Session 5 STAGED, NOT PLAYED: Jord offers a personal Hat of Disguise to the party as a gift because they previously saved his horse and strongbox, after the Crown commandeered his hotel room. Not a stock sale or restock, and no transfer until accepted in play. Edda's separately listed Hat of Disguise remains available. Preserve existing 20% Jord discount.

entries.name: Party Gear Snapshot (Advisory, Not Stock-Tailoring Rules)
entries: Arunem: regular Scale Mail, greataxe, four handaxes, Potion of Healing, Oil of Slipperiness, scroll of Lesser Restoration. Pepper: Chain Shirt, shield, mace, two shortswords, Decanter of Endless Water, Potion of Climbing, and additional salvaged weapons, Holy Water and Kaleb's notebook. Jarrock: Studded Leather, two scimitars, dart, Poisoner's Kit, Thieves' Tools, potion of Healing, and ordinary adventuring supplies. Aaron's current equipment is unknown. These are references only; the shops do not stock to party demand.

Rules reminder: a Chain Shirt is AC 13 + DEX (max +2) without Stealth disadvantage, Scale Mail is AC 14 + DEX (max +2) with Stealth disadvantage, and Studded Leather is AC 12 + full DEX. An ordinary suit of Scale Mail does not upgrade Arunem, who already has one. Do not mistake magic armor's listed rarity price for a full set of custom work.
Revisiting inventory: after a party visit, edit individual quantities in this appendix or record sales in session notes. This is a reference snapshot, not a synchronized transaction system.

Cold-playtest the material, identify information the DM would reach for, and make it instantly accessible without changing the established comprehensive prep method.

trait.name: Aura of Protection
entries: While Brakkus is conscious, he and friendly creatures within 10 feet of him gain a +4 bonus to saving throws.

trait.name: Aura of Courage
entries: While Brakkus is conscious, he and friendly creatures within 10 feet of him can't be {@condition frightened}.

trait.name: Aura of Devotion
entries: While Brakkus is conscious, he and friendly creatures within 10 feet of him can't be {@condition charmed}.

trait.name: Purity of Spirit
entries: Brakkus is continuously under the effects of {@spell Protection from Evil and Good|XPHB}.

trait.name: Relentless Endurance (1/Long Rest)
entries: When Brakkus is reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, he drops to 1 hit point instead.

trait.name: Lay on Hands (80 HP/Long Rest)
entries: Brakkus has a pool of 80 hit points of healing. As an action, he can touch a creature and restore any number of hit points remaining in the pool. He can instead spend 5 points to cure one disease or neutralize one poison affecting the target.

trait.name: Fire Walker
entries: Brakkus can stand on and move across molten rock as if it were solid ground.

trait.name: Paladin Spellcasting
entries: Brakkus's spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 17, +9 to hit with spell attacks).
At will: {@spell Sacred Flame|XPHB}, {@spell Word of Radiance|XPHB}
1/Long Rest: {@spell Shield|XPHB} (from Magic Initiate)

Prepared Paladin Spells (use spell slots): {@spell Lesser Restoration|XPHB}, {@spell Zone of Truth|XPHB}, {@spell Beacon of Hope|XPHB}, {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB}, {@spell Freedom of Movement|XPHB}, {@spell Guardian of Faith|XPHB}
Spell Slots: 1st level (4), 2nd level (3), 3rd level (3), 4th level (2)

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Brakkus makes two attacks with {@item The Appendix|NCFA}.

action.name: The Appendix
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 12} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 1d8 + 7}) slashing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) radiant damage.

action.name: Divine Smite
entries: When Brakkus hits a creature with The Appendix, he can expend a spell slot to deal additional radiant damage: 2d8 with a 1st-level slot, 3d8 with a 2nd-level slot, 4d8 with a 3rd-level slot, or 5d8 with a 4th-level slot. The damage increases by 1d8 against a Fiend or Undead, subject to the normal Divine Smite maximum.

action.name: Sacred Flame
entries: One creature Brakkus can see within 60 feet must succeed on a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw or take 13 ({@damage 3d8}) radiant damage. The target gains no benefit from Half Cover or Three-Quarters Cover for this save.

action.name: Word of Radiance
entries: Each creature of Brakkus's choice within 5 feet of him must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or take 10 ({@damage 3d6}) radiant damage.

action.name: Sacred Weapon (Channel Divinity; 1/Short or Long Rest)
entries: As an action, Brakkus imbues The Appendix with positive energy for 1 minute. He adds his Charisma modifier (+4) to attack rolls made with the weapon, raising its attack bonus to +16, and the weapon emits bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for another 20 feet.

action.name: Turn the Unholy (Channel Divinity; 1/Short or Long Rest)
entries: As an action, Brakkus presents his holy symbol. Each Fiend or Undead within 30 feet that can see or hear him must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or be Turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage.

reaction.name: Shield (1/Long Rest)
entries: When Brakkus is hit by an attack roll or targeted by {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}, he casts {@spell Shield|XPHB}. Until the start of his next turn, his AC becomes 29, including against the triggering attack, and he takes no damage from Magic Missile.
Brakkus is a roughly forty-eight-year-old half-orc, retired adventurer and mercenary, and level 16 Oath of Devotion paladin of Oghma. He owns Ledger House in Bellweather and maintains it as a refuge.
Brakkus is a home-base NPC, not a companion character. His default priorities are protect civilians, stabilize downed allies, contain the threat, then defeat the aggressor.
Challenge Rating. The listed CR is provided for encounter-building purposes; Brakkus is a 16th-level paladin.

trait.name: Fey Ancestry
entries: Jaroood has advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition charmed} condition.

trait.name: Trance
entries: Jaroood does not need to sleep; magic cannot put him to sleep, and he can finish a Long Rest with 4 hours of trance.

trait.name: High Elf Magic (Intelligence; spell save DC 13)
entries: Jaroood can cast {@spell Prestidigitation|XPHB} at will. He can cast {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} and {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} once each without a spell slot, regaining each use when he finishes a Long Rest.

trait.name: Crown Administrator
entries: Jaroood has operational authority over Cardon Weavehouse's employees, work orders, assessments, and releases. This authority is legal and social, not mind control or a combat ability.

action.name: Rapier
entries: {@atk m} {@hit 3} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d8 + 1}) piercing damage.

Jaroood is a wealthy, royal-appointed high elf administrator of the Crown's Cardon Weavehouse, with complete operational authority. He believes forced indenture is justified and receives 10% of new debt assessed against each worker. He is brave in the safety of his office and deferential to the Crown, not an adventuring combatant.

item.name: The Appendix
entries: You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic longsword.
On a hit, the weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d4} radiant damage.
The Appendix was given to Brakkus Ledgerhelm by High Justiciar Vance Halford and named in honor of Elena's love of books.
The item does not require attunement.
